text:
nisha: Hey team — first week question. Trying to run the quickstart locally and I'm getting 429s when I switch from the sandbox key to our hosted key. Anyone know if I'm supposed to use a local proxy for hosted keys?

sam: Hi! For local dev we usually point hosted requests through the dev proxy if you need to hit internal-only routes, but you shouldn't need it just to call the hosted API. Which 429 are you seeing (rate limit vs quota)?

nisha: It says "rate_limited: too many requests". I'm doing a bunch of streaming tests from my laptop (curl + --no-buffer). Might be hitting concurrent connection limits.

devon: Sandbox limits are tighter than hosted. Sandbox: small burst, ~=60 req/min and 3 streaming conns (approx). Hosted: higher throughput but still per-account rate limiting. If you need more sandbox quota ask devex.

nisha: Ah ok. I'm also trying to wire this into CI. We're considering storing HOSTED key in CI, but worried about exposing it to PRs. Any best practice?

maria: For CI use a scoped CI key or sandbox key where possible. In our org we create project-specific sandbox keys for tests and a short-lived hosted token for production deploys. In GitHub Actions set env REDWOOD_API_KEY in repo secrets and restrict to main branch for deploy jobs.

sam: Also consider using the local replay proxy during PRs (dev-proxy) so you record golden responses and avoid calling the API on every run. Saves quota and avoids flapping 429s in tests.

nisha: Can you paste the proxy curl example?

sam: Sure — example:

```bash
# proxy mode (records/serves)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hello"}' \n  http://localhost:8080/v1/generate

# direct hosted call
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

devon: Also note streaming can be heavier: keep connection reuse, smaller parallelism, and exponential backoff on 429s. If you need sustained parallel streams in sandbox, file a quota request to <@devex>.

nisha: Thanks — how do I file the request? I couldn't find the form.

maria: Ping <@devex> in slack with what you need (num conns, rps, duration). They usually ask for a short justification and team name. If urgent, open a ticket in Support and tag "sandbox-quota".

devex-bot: New quota requests may take 1-2 business days. For emergencies DM @devex lead.

nisha: Super helpful — I'll try proxying tests and open a request if needed. One last thing: is there a recommended env var name scheme?

sam: We use REDWOOD_API_KEY for hosted, REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY for sandbox, and REDWOOD_PROXY_URL if using local proxy. Keep hosted keys out of forks and PRs.

nisha: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
